newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX May COB electricity ends lower, May PV flat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX May COB electricity ends lower, May PV flat.

text.p: NYMEX May California-Oregon (COB) electricity futures settled a touch lower Monday, while the May Palo Verde (PV) contract finished unchanged from last Thursday's settlement.

News of an unplanned outage at the 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyone nuclear power unit 2 in central California gave the complex an early boost following the three-day Easter weekend, brokers and traders said.
NYMEX was closed Friday in observance of Good Friday.
But nearby months softened when the operator Pacific Gas & Electric Co said the Diablo Canyon 2 shutdown that began Saturday would only last until middle of this week,
"That's basically negated because it's shortlived," said a Houston futures trader, referring to the outage.
A late sell-off in futures was cushioned by strength in cash power prices and forecasts of snow and much colder weather in the western U.S. for much of the week.
There was also paper maneuvering of second-quarter 1997 positions when April 1 delivery begins tomorrow, brokers and traders said.
Day-ahead electricity prices for firm, peak delivery at the COB rose 50-75 cents to $11.75-12.75 a megawatt hour (MWh), while those at PV firmed 25-50 cents to $14.75-15.50. May
COB settled down two cents at $10.68 after posting a high at $10.90. June COB ended up eight cents at $11.03. Other COB months finished down 10 cents to up 25 cents.
May PV settled unchanged at $15.20 after traded between $15.10 and $15.35. June PV ended up five cents at $16.26. Other active PV contracts finished three to 16 cents higher.
Market sources said the complex would likely test the upper end of today's ranges Tuesday on the outlook of winter-like weather returning in the West.
In addition to Diablo Canyon 2, the 750 MW unit 2 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant in Nevada was shut Saturday for planned maintenance. The unit would stay down until May 11.

The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington shut since last Thursday for maintenance. A 750 MW unit at the Navajo coal-fired plant in Arizona was heard still idled for repairs which could take as long as two weeks.

Those outages were offset by the return of the 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear unit 3 in Arizona, 1,070 MW San Onofre nuclear unit 2 in southern California and increased power flow on the Pacific Intertie.
Late last week, capacity on the Intertie's high-voltage power transmission lines, linking the Northwest to Southern California, was increased about 20 percent to 6,250 MW.
NYMEX estimated 243 COB and 219 PV contracts were sold, compared with Thursday's 235 COB and 463 PV lots.
